Full Title: Homogeneity and Best Practice Analyses in Hospital Performance Management: An Analytical Framework
Authors: M. Zarrin, J. Schoenfelder, J. O. Brunner
Research Objective: Address hospital structural heterogeneity to benchmark operational best practices across facilities
Dataset and Methodology: Self-organizing maps (SOM) clustering combined with multi-layer perceptron neural networks and DEA on 1,100+ German hospitals
Main Findings: Clustering hospitals prior to efficiency frontier evaluation eliminates structural bias and produces more realistic operational targets
Limitations: Assumes rigid cluster boundaries; high sensitivity to input feature weighting
Relevance to This Project: Provides methodological foundation for segmenting hospitals by size and case volume before comparing operational efficiency

Full Title: An innovative patient clustering method using data envelopment Analysis–Discriminant analysis and artificial neural networks: A case study in healthcare systems
Authors: S. Yousefi, R. F. Saen, H. Shabanpour, K. Ghods
Research Objective: Develop multi-criteria clustering framework for hospital patient and resource efficiency grouping
Dataset and Methodology: DEA discriminant analysis coupled with artificial neural network clustering on tertiary care hospital admissions
Main Findings: Clustering on non-linear operational inputs isolates high-cost resource consumers and informs departmental capacity allocation
Limitations: Computationally complex and sensitive to small sample shifts across specialized departments
Relevance to This Project: Demonstrates validity of combining capacity utilization indicators with unsupervised groupings to reveal operational bottlenecks

Full Title: Assessing resource allocation based on workload: a data envelopment analysis study on clinical departments in a class a tertiary public hospital in China
Authors: X. Hao, L. Han, D. Zheng, et al.
Research Objective: Evaluate relationship between operational workload, staffing, and bed capacity allocation
Dataset and Methodology: DEA and hierarchical clustering on inpatient admissions, bed occupancy rates, and clinician hours across hospital departments
Main Findings: Substantial resource imbalances occur between high-turnover acute units and chronic bed units; clustering separates high-efficiency from low-utilization wards
Limitations: Single-center dataset limits generalizability across diverse geographical hospital systems
Relevance to This Project: Directly informs our feature design: bed occupancy rate, staffed-to-available beds ratio, and length of stay as utilization drivers

Full Title: Private hospitals in low- and middle-income countries: a typology using the cluster method, the case of Morocco
Authors: A. Benmoussa, M. Jouhadi, K. Benhida, et al.
Research Objective: Establish empirical typology of private healthcare facilities based on capacity, governance, and operational scale
Dataset and Methodology: K-Means and hierarchical agglomerative clustering on multi-dimensional administrative records of private hospital facilities
Main Findings: Identified distinct hospital archetypes: large multi-specialty centers, specialized surgical clinics, and low-bed regional facilities with differing cost structures
Limitations: Cross-sectional survey design lacking multi-quarter longitudinal financial reporting
Relevance to This Project: Direct benchmark for our 3-algorithm clustering approach to identify structural archetypes among California healthcare facilities

Full Title: Optimal Ambulance Positioning for Road Accidents With Deep Embedded Clustering
Authors: D. D. Desai, J. Dey, S. K. Satapathy, S. Mishra, S. N. Mohanty, P. Mishra, S. K. Panda
Research Objective: Evaluate spatial and capacity clustering algorithms to optimize emergency healthcare resource allocation
Dataset and Methodology: Comparative evaluation of K-Means, Agglomerative clustering, GMM, and Deep Embedded Clustering on regional accident and hospital demand data
Main Findings: K-Means and hierarchical linkages provide strong interpretability and competitive cluster separation compared to complex black-box architectures
Limitations: Does not evaluate hospital internal financial balance sheets
Relevance to This Project: Validates Scikit-learn baseline clustering algorithms (K-Means and Hierarchical) for healthcare resource optimization

Full Title: Unsupervised clustering analysis of trauma and non-trauma centers using hospital features including surgical care
Authors: A. Vosoughi, C. E. Jones, T. P. Cooper, et al.
Research Objective: Discover latent groupings of acute trauma facilities using structural, volume, and payer-mix features
Dataset and Methodology: Unsupervised K-Means clustering, PCA dimensionality reduction, and Silhouette analysis on multi-state hospital facility features
Main Findings: Facilities cluster naturally into tertiary high-volume regional centers, community hospitals, and rural access facilities with distinct financial vulnerability profiles
Limitations: Payer mix fluctuations between quarters can introduce minor cluster boundary drift
Relevance to This Project: Directly mirrors our study's use of PCA visualization, Silhouette validation, and multi-dimensional hospital profiling

Full Title: Association of measured quality with financial health among U.S. hospitals
Authors: K. E. Joynt Maddox, R. E. Reid, J. M. Bleser, et al.
Research Objective: Examine structural links between hospital operating margins, asset capitalization, and clinical care quality
Dataset and Methodology: Multilevel modeling and financial ratio clustering on CMS and HCRIS hospital datasets across 3,000+ US hospitals
Main Findings: Facilities with negative operating margins frequently suffer from lower bed occupancy and disproportionately high fixed expense ratios rather than low clinical demand
Limitations: Focuses on Medicare/Medicaid regulatory data rather than state quarterly disclosures
Relevance to This Project: Supports our use of operating margin, expense-to-revenue ratio, and asset volume as core financial indicators

Full Title: Measurement of the operational efficiency of tertiary public hospitals in western China: Evidence from Guangxi from 2019 to 2022
Authors: Y. Qin, X. Wei, M. Liang, et al.
Research Objective: Track post-pandemic shifts in hospital operational efficiency, bed utilization, and financial sustainability
Dataset and Methodology: Longitudinal two-stage DEA and agglomerative hierarchical clustering on hospital inputs (beds, equipment, staff) and outputs (discharges, revenues)
Main Findings: Hierarchical clustering revealed a widening efficiency divergence between high-asset urban medical centers and resource-constrained regional hospitals
Limitations: Self-reported administrative figures may exhibit reporting lags
Relevance to This Project: Validates the inclusion of multi-period quarterly reporting to capture dynamic shifts in hospital cost recovery

Full Title: Clusters of medical specialties around patients with multimorbidity – employing fuzzy c-means clustering to explore multidisciplinary collaboration
Authors: K. Vluggen, H. Vrijhoef, D. Ruwaard, et al.
Research Objective: Identify clinical service clustering patterns to guide hospital department integration and resource sharing
Dataset and Methodology: Fuzzy C-Means clustering and internal validation indices on longitudinal inpatient electronic health records
Main Findings: Identified tightly coupled departmental clusters that drive the majority of hospital inpatient bed-days and pharmacy expenditures
Limitations: Does not account for institutional capital investment or debt servicing burdens
Relevance to This Project: Highlights that inpatient bed-days and length of stay are primary physical drivers of overall hospital operational expenditures

Full Title: Patient satisfaction – results of cluster analysis of Finnish patients
Authors: P. Jousilahti, H. Kautiainen, E. Mantyselka, et al.
Research Objective: Classify healthcare facility service consumers using unsupervised clustering of operational touchpoints
Dataset and Methodology: K-Means clustering with Elbow method and Davies-Bouldin index validation on nationwide healthcare utilization surveys
Main Findings: Service satisfaction and operational efficiency closely track outpatient visit intensity and facility responsiveness
Limitations: Survey data prone to subjective recall bias compared to audited financial records
Relevance to This Project: Confirms the utility of Davies-Bouldin Index and Elbow analysis for unsupervised cluster parameter selection

Full Title: Using Medical Data and Clustering Techniques for a Smart Healthcare System
Research Objective: Optimize medical resource allocation and patient monitoring using density and distance-based clustering
Dataset and Methodology: Comparative analysis of K-Means and DBSCAN algorithms on hospital patient admission and utilization records
Main Findings: DBSCAN effectively identifies outlier records and noise points without imposing spherical cluster assumptions on non-Gaussian healthcare distributions
Limitations: High dimensional feature spaces lead to metric sparsity in DBSCAN epsilon parameter selection
Relevance to This Project: Justifies our implementation of DBSCAN alongside K-Means to identify non-standard hospital facility profiles and statistical outliers

Full Title: Latent space representation of electronic health records for patient profiling and operational clustering
Authors: Y. Jiang, T. Chen, X. Liu, et al.
Research Objective: Map high-dimensional hospital operational and diagnostic indicators into interpretable latent feature clusters
Dataset and Methodology: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) combined with K-Means and Calinski-Harabasz evaluation on hospital operational logs
Main Findings: Unsupervised latent embedding reduces multicollinearity between financial volume features and isolates independent operational drivers
Limitations: Latent components may lose immediate clinical nomenclature if unmapped to physical variables
Relevance to This Project: Directly guides our feature engineering and PCA 2D analytical visualization in the Streamlit dashboard

Full Title: Machine learning approaches to predict healthcare attendance and operational capacity utilization
Authors: F. Piccialli, V. S. Di Cola, A. Giampaolo, et al.
Research Objective: Segment outpatient and inpatient capacity utilization patterns to forecast facility workload
Dataset and Methodology: Unsupervised clustering followed by supervised ensemble learning on multi-year Italian hospital utilization databases
Main Findings: Hospital operating schedules and outpatient-to-inpatient ratios are critical predictors of capacity bottlenecks and revenue fluctuations
Limitations: Regional demographic shifts were not explicitly parameterized in the unsupervised stage
Relevance to This Project: Supports our feature engineering of Outpatient-to-Inpatient visit ratios and occupancy rates as primary utilization levers

Full Title: Hospital bed utilization and cost efficiency dynamics in post-pandemic healthcare networks
Research Objective: Quantify the impact of fixed-cost hospital bed capacity on financial resilience and cost-per-case across healthcare systems
Dataset and Methodology: Stochastic frontier analysis combined with K-Means facility clustering on German and European hospital financial panels
Main Findings: Facilities maintaining bed occupancy between 75-85% achieved optimal cost efficiency; underutilized facilities experienced sharp margin deterioration
Limitations: Data aggregated annually, obscuring intra-year seasonal quarterly shocks
Relevance to This Project: Directly supports our candidate indicators: Revenue per Available Bed, Expense per Available Bed, and Occupancy Rate

Full Title: Digital health capabilities and hospital operational efficiency: An empirical evaluation using cluster benchmarking
Authors: P. Khuntia, M. Tanniru, J. K. Weiner
Research Objective: Evaluate how capital investments in health IT systems segment hospitals into distinct operational efficiency tiers
Dataset and Methodology: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering with Ward's linkage and Silhouette coefficient validation on AHA and HIMSS hospital datasets
Main Findings: Hospitals cluster into distinct digital capability tiers where higher capital expenditure correlates with improved outpatient-to-inpatient transitions
Limitations: Cross-sectional dataset did not permit tracking long-term return on capital investments
Relevance to This Project: Affirms the use of Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering with Ward linkage as an interpretable model for hospital segmentation
